items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: In October 1955, I played a two days jazz festival in Lyon which featured Sydney Bechet, Chet Baker and myself.

ctx.x: A month or so after I had come home, a drummer by the name of Lee Rainey asked me to play for a dance with him in a small town up state Ohio. Lee was an amateur drummer but he had played with Clarence Page at times. I accepted the engagement and had learnt the "Tin Roof Blues" well enough to make Lee compliment me on the way I played it, and we played it a few times that night.

A few nights later, there was a dance at the Sterling Hotel and the band was a pick up, one that was being lead by a trumpet player named Chet. He had played in Chicago for a long time and he was a good trumpet player. I never knew why he came back to Cincinnati. Actually he lived across the river in Covington but worked in Cincinnati most of the time.

Lee Rainey was the drummer that night and I came into the dance hall with my horn. When Lee saw me, he asked Chet if I could play "Tin Roof Blues" with the band. Chet looked at me and I suppose he could tell from experience that I was not good enough to play with him, so he told Lee; no, because the music was sounding bad enough already.
